text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: DETECTED high tail latency and OOMs on continuous-batcher pool (us-west-2) — 8 nodes with paging spikes, 30% request failures, GPU OOM on pod batcher-rt-42. Metrics: batching_queue_length +400% in 3m, kvcache growth > 90GB, host swap activity. Pager: #pager-1832
Maya: saw the alert. I'm oncall. prioritizing customer impact and containment. Jun, can you grab kernel/pod logs?
Jun: grabbing logs now. I see repeated `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` followed by `OOM killer` messages. stack trace from runtime attached below.
Jun: ```
2026-06-12 03:14:12.341 INFO continuous-batcher: enqueue size=4096
2026-06-12 03:14:12.342 WARN kvcache: growth to 92GB, evicting=0
2026-06-12 03:14:12.355 ERROR runtime: cuda: kernel panic at launch, sigsegv
2026-06-12 03:14:12.356 CRITICAL containerd: oom kill process pid=4721
```
Jun: root cause looks like unbounded batch accumulation + kvcache never evicting for some request pattern (long prefix reuse). paging followed by GPU OOM.
Priya: agree. Paging -> heavy host swap -> container OOM. We should immediately reduce batch formation window and disable kvcache prefetch for affected nodes.
Maya: action plan: 1) throttle incoming traffic to batchers (route to fallback CPU model), 2) reduce `batch.window_ms` from 50 -> 10 on the pool, 3) disable kv-prefetch on pool, 4) drain the worst nodes and restart pods. Do we have an automated policy for fallback? deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: Fallback route configured: route(s) for model: redwood/llama-small -> redwood/llama-small-cpu. Traffic shift API: POST /routing/shifts {"from":"continuous-batcher","to":"cpu-fallback","pct":50}
Maya: initiating 50% shift to cpu-fallback now.
Maya: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/routing/shifts -d '{"from":"continuous-batcher","to":"cpu-fallback","pct":50}'` -> 200 OK :thumbsup:
Carlos: Customer impact: we just got an inbound support ticket from AcmeCorp reporting 5-10x latency on generation endpoints. They're on Dedicated us-west pool. I'll notify them that we're mitigating and will follow up.
Jun: lowering batching window on live config registry: `rctl set continuous-batcher.pool.us-west.window_ms 10` -> applied. Watching queue length.
Jun: disabling kv-prefetch: `rctl set continuous-batcher.pool.us-west.kv_prefetch false` -> applied.
Maya: starting node drain on node usw-batcher-09 which shows most OOMs.
Maya: `kubectl drain usw-batcher-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30` (evicting pods)
Priya: also patch the admission to cap batch size at 2048 tokens immediately so we don't re-accumulate.
Jun: applied `config override: continuous-batcher.max_batch_tokens=2048`.
Nikhil: I'm taking the next watch. If things still degrade, I'll scale out fallback pool and prepare to force traffic to Dedicated CPU.
Maya: good handoff. current numbers: queue length down from +400% to +120% in 6m, kvcache down to 60GB, rate of OOMs reduced but still seeing occasional SIGKILLs on two nodes.
Jun: I pulled core dumps; pattern shows repeated `prefetch_kv` goroutine stuck on large LRU walk. Likely a regression in the kv-eviction logic that doesn't handle large prefix trees.
Priya: can we restart runtime on the two flapping nodes instead of full node reboots? restart seems faster.
Maya: doing rolling restart of runtime container on affected pods: `kubectl rollout restart ds/continuous-batcher-runtime -n us-west --field-selector spec.nodeName=usw-batcher-07,usw-batcher-11`.
Maya: restart triggered. watching pod restarts.
deploy-bot: NOTE: a hotfix (PR #5912) was auto-deployed to staging earlier today but not to prod. Rolling back that change would be risky without test verification.
Jun: PR #5912 modifies kv eviction heuristics — could be culprit. I'd like to rollback to previous runtime on the two nodes only if we confirm it's the same build.
Maya: we don't have time for a full rollback. Containment first: reduce concurrency per node: `rctl set continuous-batcher.pool.us-west.max_concurrency 4` -> applied.
Maya: prod latency tail now trending down, customer tickets updating.
Carlos: AcmeCorp says timeout rate improved after your 50% shift, asking for ETA to full resolution. I'll tell them we're containing and will follow up within 60 minutes.
Jun: creating a diagnostic gist with core dumps and filtered logs: https://internal-gists/acme/batcher-kv-20260612
Priya: adding incident tag and starting a linked postmortem doc: `pm/INC-2026-06-12-batcher-kv-surge` (draft)
Nikhil: I'm oncall handover in 15. I'll keep an eye on OOMs, and plan to evict any pod showing repeated SIGKILLs. @Maya, handoff notes?
Maya: Handoff: reduced window -> 10ms, max_batch_tokens -> 2048, kv_prefetch disabled, 50% routing to cpu-fallback, concurrency cap 4, drained usw-batcher-09, restarted runtime on two flapping nodes. Watch kvcache size and OOMs over next 30m. If OOMs persist, escalate to infra and consider rolling back PR #5912.
Nikhil: acknowledged. I'll also prepare a safe rollback build (runtime:v2026-05-28) in case.
Maya: thanks team. tagging for post-incident follow-up: action items: 1) revert or fix kv-eviction regression (owner: Jun), 2) add circuit breaker for kvcache growth (owner: Priya), 3) improve canary test for PR #5912 (owner: eng-ci), 4) customer comms (owner: Carlos).
Carlos: I'll send AcmeCorp an interim update: acknowledging mitigation and ETA for follow-up.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: primary alert state cleared — tail latency back to acceptable, OOMs reduced to zero in last 10m. Incident severity moved from Sev2 -> Sev3. Link to timeline: https://incidents.internal/1768123456
Maya: adding analyst note: probable root cause = kv-eviction regression leading to unbounded kvcache and batch growth which triggered host paging and GPU OOMs. We'll validate in postmortem.
Nikhil: I'll run a deeper soak on staging with a reproducer that exercises long prefix reuse.
Jun: copied. I'll own the fix and follow up with patch timeline.
Maya: handoff complete. thanks all. :heart:
